subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up — p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted vs current provider)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Subject: Performance SLO follow-up — p95/p99 targets (recap + next steps)

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on performance requirements and scope a short evaluation:

Recap of your current targets we discussed:
- Workload: real-time summarization API for client dashboards (avg payload ~600 tokens)
- Concurrency goal: steady 50 qps with spikes to 150 qps
- Streaming: must support token-by-token streaming (SSE/websocket) to reduce perceived latency
- End-to-end (client -> model -> client) SLOs: p95 <= 1800ms, p99 <= 3000ms for typical inputs
- Current provider numbers (from your logs): p50 480ms, p95 1300ms, p99 2900ms (end-to-end)

Questions / assumptions I made on the call:
1) The 'end-to-end' numbers include your network and client-side processing; you also have a region preference for US-West.
2) Payload distribution: 70% short (<=400 tokens), 30% long (400-1200 tokens). Please correct me if wrong.

Proposed next steps:
1) You share a representative sample of 500 requests (anonymized) and a small test corpus — we can run a hosted evaluation against the same input distribution.
2) Redwood will run both hosted API and a "current provider parity" run to generate p50/p95/p99 and streaming throughput numbers, with the same concurrency profile.
3) We'll provide a short runbook with tuning knobs (batching, streaming buffer size, max concurrency) and estimated cost delta.

Deliverables and timeline:
- I'll send an upload link for the test corpus by EOD tomorrow (Sep 2).
- Redwood will return the evaluation report (CSV + summary + runbook) within 5 business days of receiving the sample.

If that all looks right, I'll loop in our infra lead (Aditya) to help scope the concurrency/throughput lab and Stephanie will prepare a pricing delta estimate.

Thanks — looking forward to the sample.

—

Thanks Marissa — that matches our notes. A few clarifications:
- The p95/p99 numbers I quoted are from our edge service to client (so yes, end-to-end). We see more variance during mid-day spikes.
- Token distribution: about 65% short, 25% mid, 10% long. I attached a small sample CSV with timestamps and durations.

I'm attaching the anonymized sample set (500 rows). Let me know if you need a different format.

Couple of asks on our side:
1) Can Redwood's hosted API meet p99 <= 3000ms under 150 qps while streaming? We need to understand tail behavior when many concurrent streams are active.
2) Any recommendations on max_concurrency per connection and backpressure for streaming clients.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up — p95/p99 targets (recap + next steps)

Hi Samir — thanks for the sample and CSV. We're starting a small lab run today. A few notes from the infra side:

- We'll run three scenarios: (A) Redwood hosted default config (auto-batching + KV cache), (B) Redwood hosted tuned for low latency (small batch window, aggressive prefetch), (C) Parity run with your current provider using the same client-shaped load generator.
- For streaming, we'll measure token-latency and end-to-end latency separately and correlate. Streaming adds socket overhead — we'll include a breakdown column in the CSV.
- Expected ramp: we'll test steady 50 qps and spike to 150 qps for 2-minute windows to observe tail amplification.

Initial guidance:
- Start with max_concurrency_per_instance = 8 for long requests, 16 for short requests; this keeps GPU utilization efficient without queuing too many streams.
- Use a streaming buffer window of 20ms to balance smooth token flow vs incremental latency.

I'll share the test plan and data ingestion link in the next email (attaching run scripts and expected CSV schema).

-Aditya
